sense: a sitting of a council, court or senate

evidence: Cic. de Or. 3.121: pōmerīdiāna sessiō (Lewis & Short)
Dig. 38.15.2.1: diēs sessiōnum, of a court (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Literally the act of sitting, and so a seat; Cicero uses it of an afternoon’s sitting for discussion, and of idle sitting about (sessiō Capitōlīna, Att. 14.14.2, Lewis & Short).

evidence: Traupman 180, 376: senate session, senātus; to hold a session, senātum habēre
terms.comment: The senate itself and its meeting: senātum habēre, to hold a session; senātum vocāre, to call one (Traupman).

The people seated in a court, a theatre or at the games, rather than the time they sit (Lewis & Short). For a period given to an activity, such as a training session or a lesson, Latin names the activity (see exercise, lesson).

phrases.latin: eō diē nōn fuit senātus neque posterō
phrases.english: there was no session of the senate that day, nor the next

sources: Lewis & Short: sessio · Lewis & Short: senatus · Lewis & Short: consessus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 180, 376.
